blocks.text: `docker stop` sends the stop signal (SIGTERM by default), waits a grace period (10 s default), then sends SIGKILL. `docker kill` sends SIGKILL immediately (or any signal with `-s`).

rows: App handled SIGTERM and exited cleanly
Died on SIGTERM with the default action
SIGKILL: grace period expired, docker kill, or OOM

items: Stop signal: `STOPSIGNAL` in the Dockerfile or `--stop-signal`. nginx's image uses SIGQUIT (graceful); SIGTERM is its fast shutdown.
`docker kill -s HUP nginx` sends a reload signal without stopping.
Uvicorn on SIGTERM stops accepting, drains in-flight requests, runs lifespan shutdown.
`--timeout-graceful-shutdown 20` bounds the drain; the container grace period must be longer, or SIGKILL cuts it off.
Long LLM streams are in-flight requests; budget for them.

async def lifespan(app):
    app.state.pool = await create_pool()
    yield
    await app.state.pool.close()      # runs on SIGTERM

blocks.text: Every stop taking exactly 10 s and ending in 137 means PID 1 ignores SIGTERM: shell-form CMD, entrypoint without exec, or a script with no handler.

Q: "docker stop vs docker kill?" A: "stop sends SIGTERM, waits the grace period (10 s default), then SIGKILL, allowing graceful shutdown; kill sends SIGKILL immediately with no cleanup. Stops that always take 10 s mean the app isn't receiving SIGTERM."

items: Check STOPSIGNAL for software with a different graceful signal.
